title: Client SDK: idempotent Apply Contracts and Safe Rollback for Optimize Automation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Purpose: define and implement client-side SDK contracts and helper primitives that make Optimize automation 'apply' operations safe, idempotent, and easy to integrate for customers. This ticket focuses on SDK ergonomics, local preflight checks, contract-level tokens for compare-and-apply, deterministic rollback helpers, and HTTP webhook ack semantics required by the control plane.

Background: Optimize produces batching/caching recommendations that customers can accept, schedule, or have applied automatically. Past incidents show partial applies (half-applied policies) and races between concurrent recommenders led to cost spikes and customer confusion. We need a first-class client SDK layer that encodes recommended patterns (two-phase apply, commit tokens, retries) so integrators don't have to re-implement fragile logic.

Goals:
- Define a compact idempotent Apply contract for the Control API (client SDK primitives + server expectations).
- Ship SDK helpers: preflight simulation, dry-run patch builder, optimistic-apply with commit token, and rollback helper that can undo an exact change.
- Standardize webhook acknowledgement protocol: exactly-once semantics as best-effort with at-least-once delivery handling patterns and DLQ guidance.
- Provide tests, e2e harness, and migration guide for customers currently calling the raw endpoints.

Design decisions and constraints:
- Commitment token: server returns a short-lived opaque commit_token on preflight/dry-run which must be presented for the final apply. This avoids TOCTOU races. SDK will automatically refresh tokens when stale.
- Patch model: prefer "delta patches" (add/remove/bump keys) with an exactly-applied patch ID; full-replace allowed for large rewrites but requires stronger confirmation.
- Idempotency key: client-supplied idempotency_key (UUID v4) will be accepted by server; server stores mapping for 24h. SDK will generate keys when not provided and expose hooks to surface them in logs for auditing.
- Rollback: SDK saves an exact inverse-patch object at commit time; rollback API will accept inverse patch + original commit_token to ensure authorization and auditing.
- Webhooks: webhook endpoint requires 2xx to ack; SDK will supply a recommended ack/receipt handler that replies quickly and performs heavy processing async. Include backoff and retry for transient 5xx. Recommend a DLQ for webhook bodies that repeatedly fail signature or processing.
- Observability: emit metrics: optimize.apply.latency, optimize.apply.conflicts, optimize.rollback.count, optimize.webhook.retries, optimize.webhook.dlq_count.

API shape (summary):
- POST /v1/optimize/preflight -> {recommendation_id, proposed_patch} -> 200 {commit_token, patch_id, dry_run_report}
- POST /v1/optimize/apply -> {patch_id, commit_token, idempotency_key} -> 200 {status: applied | already_applied | conflicted, applied_at, audit_id}
- POST /v1/optimize/rollback -> {audit_id, inverse_patch, idempotency_key} -> 200 {status: rolled_back | not_found | rollback_conflict}
acceptance_criteria: SDK implements preflight -> auto-commit flow with commit_token refresh when expired
SDK generates idempotency_key automatically and exposes it to logs and callbacks
Apply calls are retried safely: duplicate requests must not double-apply; server returns already_applied when appropriate
Rollback helper can reconstruct and submit inverse patch; rollback operations are idempotent
Webhook ack helper included in SDK with recommended async processing pattern and DLQ guidance
Integration tests cover race between two concurrent applies to same target and assert no partial state is left
Metrics for apply/rollback/webhook retry counts are emitted and exported to CloudWatch/Prometheus
updates: 2026-02-14: Ticket created. Initial design doc linked in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Client+SDK+Apply+Contracts
2026-02-18: Spike completed — POC for commit_token flow implemented (service + minimal Go and TypeScript SDKs). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize-sdk/pull/128

2026-02-22: Design review with PM (Lena Morales) and Security (Sanjay Rao). Security requested HMAC verification for webhook payloads and limit on commit_token TTL (default 5m). Action: add token TTL config and rotate logic in SDK.

2026-03-01: SDK prototypes refactored into 'apply' facade; added retry/backoff config and hook for custom DLQ handler. Running e2e between control-plane staging and sdk-e2e harness. Blocker: non-deterministic patch ordering in the staging runtime observed under high concurrency — mitigation drafted (server-side patch sequencing + client patch_id requirement).
risks: If commit_token TTL is too short, higher latencies may cause unnecessary failures — SDK must surface clear retry semantics and auto-refresh.
Customers running older control-plane versions will need a migration path; SDK should detect server feature flags and fallback to legacy behaviour.
Edge case: cross-customer shared resources could make undo patches unsafe; must add guardrails and confirm ownership before apply/rollback.
next_steps: Finish TypeScript and Go SDK implementations for preflight/apply/rollback and publish 0.1.0 alpha
Extend control-plane API to return patch_id and persist inverse_patch snapshot at commit time (backend ticket assigned).
Add e2e harness tests that simulate 50 concurrent apply attempts against same target and assert idempotent outcome.
Prepare migration guide and code samples for existing customers using raw endpoints.
Schedule security review follow-up with SSO/KMS team to confirm audit logging of commit_token usage and HMAC key rotation.
Add dashboard tile in Redwood Console showing pending apply_count, recent rollbacks, and DLQ size for Optimize automation.
notes: Prototype showed that storing inverse_patch as a compact JSON delta reduces rollback complexity compared to snapshotting full config (saves bandwidth and time).
Recommend default idempotency_key retention on server to 24h; make it configurable per-tenant.
Webhook recommended pattern: quick HTTP 202 + spawn worker that marks ack with audit_id after processing; if worker fails, increment webhook.retry metric and push to DLQ after N attempts.
Conformance: SDKs must expose a TestHarness utility that can run through dry-run -> apply -> rollback sequence deterministically for CI.
